transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with a really low, depressed mood and constant sadness for a very long time now. It has been going on almost every day for about two years and five months. I just really need some help because I can't seem to shake this feeling.
Have you had periods of feeling better for more than two months at a time during these two and a half years?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I don't recall having any clear periods of feeling better during this whole time. It feels like this low mood has just been constantly there.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Major Depressive Disorder", "Persistent Depressive Disorder"], but based on this conversation, the patient reports a low mood that has been present almost every day for over two years without clear periods of feeling better for more than two months, which meets the criteria for Persistent Depressive Disorder (formerly known as dysthymia). This chronic course without significant remission makes Major Depressive Disorder less likely as a primary diagnosis, although it could co-occur; however, there is currently insufficient evidence for a superimposed major depressive episode. Therefore, Persistent Depressive Disorder is the most accurate diagnosis at this time.
